summary: Draft decreasing strict real-PL regularization for arbitrary classical psh on separated smooth boundaryless second-countable strict curves. Finite separable mesh realization, formal-model membership and Galois descent repair the invalid identification of Thuillier-lisse with strict real-PL. No sharp curve range is claimed.
detailedSummary: Over a complete nontrivially valued field, arbitrary classical psh functions, including permitted minus-infinity values, admit a local decreasing sequence under the stated curve and topology hypotheses. Thuillier supplies finite continuous lisse functions f_S on a compact strict domain Y, subharmonic on its ordinary interior W. Rational-sublevel Lindelof extraction supplies f_n without continuity of the target. Chord interpolation after finite separable mesh realization gives f_n <= g_n <= f_n+2^-n. Integral formal-model star functions prove actual strict real-PL membership; Galois averaging and GJR Corollary 5.12 descend it. The functions q_n=g_n+2^-n are semipositive, decrease because q_(n+1)<=f_(n+1)+2^-n<=q_n, and converge pointwise, including at minus-infinity points. No residue characteristic, perfection, genus or residue Picard-torsion restriction is added. This is an unverified draft proof of a sufficient curve range, not the original higher-dimensional characterization.
text:
Draft theorem A. Let K be a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field. Let C be a separated, smooth, strictly K-analytic space of pure dimension one. Smooth means rig-smooth and without relative boundary over K; such curves are good. Assume C is second countable. For every classical curve-test psh h:C→R∪{−∞} and every b∈C, there is one fixed ordinary open neighbourhood W of b and finite semipositive strict GJR real-PL functions q_n on W decreasing pointwise to h. Finite continuous targets additionally have uniform convergence on compact subsets. This is a draft mathematical proof, not an independent correctness certificate.

Checked foundations. Gubler–Rabinoff, arXiv:2506.13548v2, Definition 3.4 and 3.4.1 identify the curve-test class on connected smooth strict curves with Thuillier subharmonic functions or the constant −∞. Proposition 3.5(7–9) supplies scalar compatibility, functoriality and finiteness at non-rig-points unless the function is identically −∞ on the relevant interior irreducible component. Definition 4.1 quantifies over all analytic extension fields and analytic curves. Proposition 4.2 gives classical psh pullbacks. Theorem 4.3 says an already strict real-PL function on a good strict space over a nontrivially valued field is semipositive exactly when it is classical psh. These statements were checked on PDF pages 10–11 and 21–23, with relevant proofs on pages 18–19.

Thuillier’s public HAL thesis distinguishes the all-domain site X_G from the strict rigid site X_R on printed pages 19–20. Definition 3.2.1, printed page 68, uses arbitrary affinoid domains for lisse functions. Proposition 3.2.4 and its proof, printed page 69, supply a finite separable extension and a semistable skeletal description on a compact strict domain; the proof explicitly treats φ∈A^0(Y) for compact Y. Proposition 2.2.21, printed pages 42–43, describes scalar extension of a semistable skeleton as a surjective G-local isomorphism of weighted integral polyhedra. The graph Laplacian is the sum of weighted outgoing slopes, as defined on printed pages 5–7. Theorem 3.2.10, printed pages 73–75, identifies the Laplacian of a skeletal pullback on Y minus its actual boundary with this graph Laplacian. Proposition 3.4.4, printed pages 90–91, characterizes subharmonic lisse functions by nonnegative Laplacian. Theorem 3.4.2 and its proof, printed pages 89–90, construct a decreasing family, not a sequence, of finite continuous lisse functions on compact Y, subharmonic on Y\∂Y, with the required pointwise infimum. Corollary 3.4.5 gives scalar pullback of subharmonicity.

Gubler–Jell–Rabinoff, arXiv:2111.05741, Definition 5.1 uses strict analytic domains for real-PL membership. Sections 5.5–5.7 give integral model functions and their real linear combinations. Proposition 5.11 gives descent under finite flat surjective morphisms with divisible coefficients. Corollary 5.12 gives descent across a completion of an algebraic field extension; its finite case is explicitly deduced from 5.11. Sections 15.3–15.4 give admissible subdivisions when coordinates lie in the actual value group and vertical Cartier model functions for piecewise (Z,Γ)-linear skeletal functions. Section 15.8 gives strict domains for the corresponding subgraphs. Lemma 5.4 and Proposition 7.6 preserve strict membership and semipositivity under morphism and scalar pullbacks. Relevant checked PDF pages are 31–36, 45–47 and 77–80.

The cached March Gubler–Rabinoff paper, arXiv:2503.05513, labels its curve comparison Proposition 5.1 and its curve-testing comparison Corollary 5.4, on pages 15–17. The June proof refers to earlier labels 3.1 and 3.5. The actual cached statements, rather than an inferred missing label, were checked. Berkovich PMIHES 78 (1993), Proposition 1.5.5, printed pages 34–35, identifies relative domain interior with ordinary topological interior and gives the good composition rule used below.

The lisse/strict distinction is indispensable. GJR Example 5.3, page 31, takes value group Q and shows that max{π log|T|+1,0} has a corner at tropical coordinate 1/π and is not strict real-PL, although both inputs are strict real-PL. Thus arbitrary real maxima cannot be used to assert strict membership. GJR Proposition 15.11, pages 80–81, produces a decreasing weakly smooth net and explicitly permits subdivisions that are not formal-model subdivisions. It is not invoked as a strict real-PL regularization theorem.

One-sided approximation lemma. Suppose Y⊂C is a compact strictly affinoid domain, W=Y\∂_K Y, and f∈A^0(Y) is finite continuous on Y and subharmonic on W. For every ε>0, there is a continuous strict real-PL g on all of Y, semipositive on W, satisfying f≤g≤f+ε on Y.

First obtain, from the compact-domain argument of Thuillier Proposition 3.2.4, a finite separable extension L/K, a simply semistable formal model of Y_L, a finite weighted skeleton Σ, a retraction τ, and a continuous piecewise affine real F with f_L=F∘τ. Replace L by its finite Galois closure and base change the model. Nodal charts xy=a retain their equations after extension. Retractions commute with extension: on a nodal tube they use −log|x|, and on a smooth tube they retract to the corresponding component vertex. Thuillier Proposition 2.2.21 supplies the weighted skeletal compatibility. Lifted edges retain their affine coordinates and slopes.

Let M_0 bound the absolute values of the finitely many slopes of F. Choose a mesh scale δ with M_0δ<ε; choosing δ<ε/(M_0+1) includes M_0=0. Write Γ_L=−log|L*|. Original edge lengths lie in Γ_L. If Γ_L is dense, choose such a positive δ in Γ_L. Cut each edge at successive multiples of δ, retaining its other endpoint. If Γ_L=γZ is discrete, choose an arbitrarily large integer N prime to char K when that characteristic is positive, and take δ=γ/N. These cut coordinates belong to (1/N)Γ_L. They become actual value-group coordinates after adjoining roots of finitely many scalars: X^N−a is separable because N is invertible in the field. Mixed characteristic requires no residue-characteristic restriction.

For strict star domains, choose an integer D≥5 prime to char K when necessary. Also include auxiliary coordinates at fractions 1/D, 2/D, (D−2)/D and (D−1)/D of every mesh segment. All the finitely many coordinates have denominators prime to the field characteristic. Adjoining appropriate roots realizes them in a single finite separable extension; take a finite Galois closure M/K containing L. In the dense case the additional D-th roots suffice for these auxiliary fractions. Base change the model to M. Every replacement and auxiliary coordinate now lies in the actual Γ_M. Original irrational breakpoints need not become legal vertices: they are replaced by the mesh, not asserted to be strict.

Write F_M for the lifted potential. Scalar subharmonicity, Thuillier Theorem 3.2.10 and Proposition 3.4.4 imply that F_M is convex on each original edge and has nonnegative weighted outgoing-slope sum at every original vertex outside the graph boundary. Define G to equal F_M at mesh and original vertices and to be affine between consecutive mesh vertices. At isolated vertices retain F_M. On a segment [s,t],
G(z)=((t−z)F_M(s)+(z−s)F_M(t))/(t−s).
Convexity gives G≥F_M. The Lipschitz bound gives 0≤G(z)−F_M(z)≤M_0(t−s)≤M_0δ<ε.

At an original vertex, the chord slope along every outgoing edge is at least the original outgoing derivative. Positive edge weights therefore preserve nonnegative weighted slope sum. At a replacement vertex in an edge, successive chord slopes are nondecreasing, and both halves have the same edge weight. Consequently all new Laplacian masses are nonnegative. No positivity condition is imposed at the actual boundary vertices. The skeletal lisse construction and graph Laplacian formula give g_M^0=G∘τ_M, continuous on Y_M and subharmonic on W_M, satisfying f_M≤g_M^0≤f_M+ε.

Actual strict membership is a separate argument. Cover each mesh vertex by its closed star running a fraction 2/D into each adjacent mesh segment, and cover the remaining edge portions by intervals with endpoints at fractions 1/D and (D−1)/D. This is a finite neighbourhood cover of the graph; parallel edges have distinct cut endpoints. Their retraction inverse images are strict analytic domains and form a G-cover of Y_M by GJR 15.3, 15.4 and 15.8. They include residual-disc tubes through the vertex stars. All subdivisions are admissible because their coordinates are actual Γ_M values, even for discrete value groups.

On an interval, G=c+at. The logarithmic annular coordinate t is integral PL up to sign and a value-group constant. Every real constant is real-PL: c=(c/log|α|)log|α| for any α∈M* with |α|≠1.

On a star centered at v, define H_e to be distance from v on the chosen arm e and zero on every other arm. Its slopes are 1 and 0; its intercepts belong to Γ_M because the center and endpoints have Γ_M coordinates. Thus it is piecewise (Z,Γ_M)-linear in GJR’s exact definition. Section 15.4 supplies a vertical Cartier divisor on an admissible formal model of the strict star domain with model function H_e∘τ_M. Sections 5.5–5.6 make this function strict integral PL. On the whole star,
G∘τ_M=G(v)+Σ_e a_e(H_e∘τ_M),
where a_e are its real outgoing slopes. Section 5.7 proves strict real-PL membership. No harmonicity or residue Picard-torsion condition is imposed on the basis functions. Their residue line bundles need not be trivial, so ordinary CLD smoothness is not asserted. Isolated vertices use the constant formula. All interval and star formulas agree on intersections because they are literally the same function G∘τ_M. This proves global strict membership on Y_M. The already proved subharmonicity then gives semipositivity on W_M by the classical/real-PL comparison.

The interpolation need not be Galois invariant. Average it:
ĝ_M=[M:K]^{-1}Σ_{σ∈Gal(M/K)}g_M^0∘σ.
Isometric semilinear automorphisms preserve strict domains, analytic units and subharmonicity. Finite positive real sums preserve subharmonicity and strict real-PL membership, using common refinements of strict G-covers. Since f_M is invariant, f_M≤ĝ_M≤f_M+ε.

This average has an actual continuous descent g on Y. Over y∈Y, the finite algebra H(y)⊗_K M is a product of finite field extensions. Normality of M/K makes the Galois action transitive on its factors, viewed through embeddings into an algebraic closure of H(y). Each factor has the unique absolute value extending that of the complete field H(y). The action is therefore transitive on the analytic fibre. The finite surjective map Y_M→Y is a closed quotient of compact Hausdorff spaces, so an invariant continuous function descends uniquely.

Apply GJR Corollary 5.12 to good strict Y, coefficient group R, and the finite complete algebraic extension M/K. It descends the proved strict M-real-PL membership to strict K-real-PL membership. Its finite case is Proposition 5.11: the projection is finite flat surjective, since on affinoid algebras tensoring with finite-dimensional M is free of rank [M:K]. This is strict descent across ground fields, not all-domain sheafification.

Classical curve scalar compatibility, GR Proposition 3.5(7), descends subharmonicity to W. Here W_M=Y_M\∂_M Y_M: both Y_M→Y and M(M)→M(K) are finite and boundaryless, and Berkovich’s good composition equality identifies the interiors first over K and then over M. GR Theorem 4.3 now proves semipositivity of g on W. Surjectivity passes the inequalities to Y. This proves the one-sided approximation lemma.

Countable extraction lemma. On a second-countable space Z, let h be upper semicontinuous and let f_i be a decreasing directed family of finite continuous functions with h=inf_i f_i. For every rational a, the open set {h<a} is the union of the open sets {f_i<a}. An open subspace of a second-countable space is Lindelof. Choose a countable subcover for each a and enumerate the union of the selected indices. Successive upper bounds in the directed set retain all previous choices and give a decreasing sequence. If h(z)<a, a selected index, and hence every sufficiently late chosen upper bound, has f_i(z)<a. All rational a>h(z) give infimum h(z); if h(z)=−∞, use all rational a. The reverse inequality follows from f_i≥h. No continuity or finite-valued hypothesis on h is used.

A countable dense subset of K supplies second countability for algebraic analytifications of finite type. A strict affinoid algebra has a countable norm-dense subset, obtained from polynomials over a countable dense subfield in a Tate presentation. Evaluation on that subset separates bounded multiplicative seminorms and induces the full topology, because | |a(x)|−|b(x)| |≤||a−b|| in the quotient Banach norm. Hence its compact spectrum embeds homeomorphically into R_{�≥0}^N and is metrizable and second countable. More precisely the product here is indexed by the natural numbers, not a finite N. An affine algebraic chart, embedded in affine space, has an exhaustion by strict affinoid intersections with polydiscs of radii R^m, with R∈|K*| and R>1. The ordinary opens where the coordinate norms are strictly smaller than R^m cover the chart and are second countable subspaces of these affinoids. A finite affine covering gives a countable ordinary open covering and a countable base for the whole analytification. Ordinary open subspaces inherit it.

Proof of theorem A. Work in the connected component of b. If h≡−∞ there, q_n=−n gives the result; constants are strict real-PL and harmonic. Otherwise GR 3.4.1 identifies h with Thuillier subharmonicity. A connected smooth curve is irreducible, and GR 3.5(9) makes h finite at all non-rig-points. Choose a connected compact strictly affinoid neighbourhood Y of b with b in its ordinary interior. Goodness and strictness supply it; an affinoid connected component can be selected by idempotents. Its boundary is the finite Shilov boundary of non-rig-points, where h is finite. Because C has no boundary, W=Y\∂_K Y is precisely the ordinary interior of Y in C, by Berkovich 1.5.5. It is one relatively compact ordinary open neighbourhood of b.

Use Thuillier Theorem 3.4.2 on this particular Y. Its proof supplies finite continuous f_S∈A^0(Y), indexed by finite S⊂I(Y) containing ∂Y, with f_S=h on S, harmonic off S, subharmonic on W, decreasing under inclusions of S, and inf_S f_S=h on W. The source’s determination lemma 3.4.1 handles rigid and type-IV values in this infimum assertion; no continuity of h is inserted. The extraction lemma gives f_n decreasing to h on W. Upper bounds here are finite unions of S, so the chosen functions remain finite continuous lisse functions on all of Y and decrease there too.

Apply the one-sided approximation lemma to f_n with ε_n=2^{-n}, always on the same Y and W. Obtain f_n≤g_n≤f_n+2^{-n}. Set q_n=g_n+2^{-n}. The shift is a strict real-PL harmonic constant. Each q_n is finite, strict real-PL and semipositive on W, and
q_{n+1}≤f_{n+1}+2^{-n}≤f_n+2^{-n}≤g_n+2^{-n}=q_n.
Moreover h≤q_n and 0≤q_n−f_n≤2^{1−n}. Thus q_n decreases pointwise to h, also when h is −∞. Extensions and models may vary with n, but every descended function has domain Y and every semipositive approximant has the same ordinary domain W.

For a finite continuous target, the increasing opens {q_n−h<η} cover any compact subset of W. Compactness supplies one index covering it, proving uniform convergence there. For any analytic K'/K, GJR 5.4 and 7.6 preserve strict membership and semipositivity of q_n∘π, and evaluation at each point gives q_n∘π↓h∘π. This pulls back an existing sequence; no extraction for arbitrary new functions over nonmetrizable extension spaces is claimed.

The complete argument is retained in P02.1-argument.md and embedded in standalone P02.1-paper.tex. Source extracts and application checks are in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. Rerun source retention with python retain_sources.py and diagnostics plus two TeX passes with python rerun.py. No unpublished book assertion is a premise. The next note uses this curve result for a higher-dimensional sector; this note does not solve original P02.1.

summary: Draft higher-dimensional sector: every arbitrary classical psh on a full projective bundle over a second-countable smooth curve descends along compact projective fibres and has local decreasing strict semipositive real-PL pullbacks. The proof requires saturated domains.
detailedSummary: For complete nontrivially valued K with a countable dense subset, a smooth connected separated algebraic curve C0, an ordinary open Omega⊂C0^an, and an algebraic bundle E of rank r+1≥2, every classical psh u on X=P(E)^an restricted to Omega equals h∘p. Scalar pullback and the published local maximum principle prove constancy on compact connected boundaryless projective H(b)-fibres. Trivialization sections prove classical psh descent and exact overlap agreement. Note n1 supplies one fixed W and q_n, and v_n=q_n∘p is globally strict real-PL and semipositive on p^-1(W), decreasing pointwise to u. Every analytic scalar extension preserves the same sequence, even without metrizability of the extension space. These are smooth normal unibranch spaces of dimension r+1, including proper projective factors. No conclusion for every arbitrary psh germ on nonsaturated fibre charts, or for arbitrary normal/unibranch spaces, follows.
text:
Draft theorem B. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, with a countable dense subset. Let C0 be a smooth connected separated algebraic curve of finite type over K, Ω⊂C0^an an ordinary open subset, and E an algebraic vector bundle of rank r+1≥2. Let p:X=P(E)^an|_Ω→Ω. For every arbitrary classical psh u:X→R∪{−∞} and every x∈X there is one fixed ordinary open neighbourhood V=p^{-1}(W) and finite semipositive strict real-PL v_n on V decreasing pointwise to u. The construction is v_n=q_n∘p, using n1. The hypothesis on K can be replaced by second countability of the relevant base curve. No continuity, invariance, finiteness, residue-genus or residue-Picard-torsion restriction is placed on u. The product Ω×(P_K^r)^an is included.

Compact constancy lemma. A classical psh function w on a connected compact boundaryless analytic space F is constant, allowing −∞. If not identically −∞, upper semicontinuity and compactness give a finite attained maximum m: local finite upper bounds have a finite subcover, and compactness gives attainment. The set {w=m} is nonempty and closed. It is open by Gubler–Rabinoff arXiv:2506.13548v2, Theorem 6.1, since every point of F is an interior point. Connectedness makes it all of F. This applies to the full classical curve-test class.

For every complete nontrivially valued H, (P_H^r)^an is compact, connected and boundaryless. Its finite standard closed unit-polydisc covering proves compactness. It is good, strict and boundaryless as an algebraic analytification, as recalled on GJR page 8. Each polydisc is connected, and any two standard charts meet at the homogeneous point with all coordinates 1.

Here is a direct polydisc connectedness proof. For a point z of the closed unit polydisc, use its coordinate values z_i in H(z). Evaluate a polynomial P(z_1+U_1,…,z_r+U_r) with the Gauss norm of polyradius s∈[0,1]. This is a multiplicative seminorm bounded by the unit-polydisc norm. At s=0 it is z. At s=1 it is the unit Gauss point, because translation by coordinates of norm at most 1, and its inverse, preserve the unit Gauss norm. For each polynomial its value is a maximum of finitely many continuous expressions in s; norm density extends continuity to the Tate algebra. Every point has a path to the Gauss point. This works over H=H(b) without a countability assumption on that fibre field.

For b∈Ω, extend scalars to H(b), then include the analytic fibre p^{-1}(b)≅(P_{H(b)}^r)^an into X_{H(b)}. This uses the H(b)-point of Ω_{H(b)} over b. GR Proposition 4.2 makes the scalar pullback and its restriction classical psh. The compact constancy lemma therefore proves that u is constant on the entire fibre, including non-rigid points. Define h(b) to be this value. Then u=h∘p.

On an ordinary open base set U where the projective bundle trivializes, choose its analytic section s_U given by [1:0:…:0]. We have h|_U=u∘s_U, so h is upper semicontinuous and classical psh there by GR Proposition 4.2. Sections from different trivializations have the same u-value over every point, by fibre constancy. They agree exactly on overlaps. Classical psh sheafiness proves that h is classical psh on Ω, retaining its possible discontinuities and −∞ values. No quotient-topology assumption for this descent is needed because there are local sections.

The field hypothesis makes Ω second countable by the affinoid/algebraic argument in n1. Apply n1 to h at b=p(x), obtaining one W and one q_n. Let V=p^{-1}(W) and v_n=q_n∘p. This is an ordinary open neighbourhood of x. GJR Lemma 5.4(1) proves actual strict real-PL membership; Proposition 7.6(1) proves semipositivity. These results require good strict spaces but do not require p to be finite. Pointwise evaluation gives v_{n+1}(y)≤v_n(y) and lim_n v_n(y)=h(p(y))=u(y). The functions are defined globally on all of V. Every projective trivialization sees the same q_n∘p, so all chart overlaps agree term by term. There are no separately selected chart approximants requiring a gluing argument. If h is finite continuous, a compact subset of V has compact image in W, and the locally uniform conclusion of n1 pulls back.

These are genuine higher-dimensional normal unibranch examples. P(E) is smooth over K and has dimension r+1. Berkovich PMIHES 78 (1993), Corollary 2.2.7, printed pages 42–43, passes regularity and normality to the algebraic analytification and hence its ordinary open subspace X. Regular local rings are normal domains; a normal local ring is unibranch because its normalization is itself. No normalization descent occurs in this proof. Nontrivial projective-bundle transition functions are permitted. For example A_K^{1,an}×(P_K^r)^an has the result for all its globally defined classical psh functions, including pullbacks of log|t−a| with value −∞ at their poles. No torus invariance hypothesis is imposed.

Scalar compatibility. For any analytic extension K'/K, let π:V_{K'}→V be the projection. GJR 5.4(2) and 7.6(2) make v_n∘π strict real-PL and semipositive over K'. At each y', v_n(π(y')) decreases to u(π(y')). GR Proposition 4.2(5) also verifies that the target pullback remains classical psh. These formulas commute with p_{K'} and all projective coordinate transitions. Finite separable fields used in n1 only construct descended functions; they do not replace the assertion about every analytic extension by one about algebraic extensions. The extension space may be nonmetrizable. We pull back an existing sequence and do not claim countable extraction for arbitrary new starting functions over K'.

The overlap conclusion is local in the precise requested sense. A construction at one point supplies one sequence globally on W and one globally on p^{-1}(W), with exact compatibility throughout its charts. Independently constructed sequences near different base points need not agree on their common base open set. No global sequence on an arbitrary union of such neighbourhoods is asserted.

The domain must contain whole projective fibres. A psh function defined only on a nonsaturated ordinary open chart need not descend. Thus this is an unrestricted starting-function sufficient sector on the displayed X, not a characterization of every arbitrary higher-dimensional psh germ. The complete proof and remaining obligations are retained in P02.1-argument.md, with standalone embedding P02.1-paper.tex. Rerun python retain_sources.py and python rerun.py in the workspace.

summary: Original P02.1 remains open here. Necessary F_sigma sublevels and analytic-retraction tests are proved; strict real maxima and nonsaturated or boundary shortcuts can fail. No sharp analytic regularization counterexample is supplied. Required artifacts and successful two-pass builds are retained.
detailedSummary: A decreasing sequence of finite continuous approximants forces every strict sublevel set to be F_sigma. Pullback through an analytic section gives a necessary retraction test. GJR Example 5.3 is a strict-membership counterexample at an irrational tropical corner, not a counterexample to regularization. A varying log|z1| on an affine projective-fibre chart defeats fibre constancy on nonsaturated domains; a closed disc defeats compact constancy if its actual boundary is retained. General higher-dimensional germs, sharp necessity/failure, singular normalization descent and unrestricted non-second-countable extraction remain unresolved. Seven supplied source hash pairs and 57 literal pages were checked; eight finite rational graph diagnostics passed. Both final TeX passes returned 0, each with one underfull hbox diagnostic and no label warning. These observations do not certify mathematics; candidate is false.
text:
The results of n1 and n2 do not provide the original characterization. The following necessity statements and limitations distinguish proved facts from shortcut failures.

Sequence obstruction. If u=inf_n v_n on an ordinary neighbourhood V, with all v_n finite continuous, then for every real a,
{u<a}=⋃_{n,k≥1}{v_n≤a−1/k}.
If u(x)<a, some v_n(x)<a and then some k supplies the displayed closed-set inequality; the converse is immediate. Every set on the right is closed in V. Thus strict sublevel sets must be F_sigma. Strict real-PL functions are continuous, so this is necessary for the requested sequence. On a nonmetrizable space, upper semicontinuity alone does not supply it. No classical psh function violating this condition is constructed here; it is not claimed to be a sharp analytic failure criterion. The Lindelof extraction of n1 is sufficient, and does not prove countable dense fields necessary.

Retraction necessity. Suppose analytic maps s:B→X and p:X→B satisfy p∘s=id. If every h∘p has local decreasing semipositive strict real-PL regularization near s(b), pull its approximants back by s on the ordinary open s^{-1}(V). GJR 5.4 and 7.6 prove strict membership and semipositivity; pointwise evaluation proves the same decreasing limit h. Therefore the base curve remains a genuine necessary test for a projective bundle with sections. This is a functorial necessity statement, not a classification of all good strict spaces.

Strict-max membership counterexample. GJR Example 5.3, PDF page 31, uses additive value group Q and the rank-one torus. The two functions π log|T|+1 and 0 are strict real-PL, while their maximum has tropical potential max{−πt+1,0} and corner t=1/π∉Q. Strict affinoid tropical intervals have rational vertices, and the published example concludes that this maximum is not strict real-PL. It is classical psh by the classical max/cone property, since log|T| is pluriharmonic. This refutes closure under arbitrary real maxima and the all-domain-lisse identification. It does not show failure of decreasing strict real-PL regularization: the mesh repair in n1 deliberately avoids that inference.

Saturation and actual boundaries. On an affine coordinate chart in a projective fibre, log|z_1| is classical psh and varies along that fibre. The chart omits the hyperplane at infinity, so its fibre portion is not compact. Compact fibre constancy therefore cannot descend every arbitrary psh germ from such a chart. This is a counterexample to the descent shortcut, not to regularization. A compact closed disc also has nonconstant classical psh functions, for example max{log|T|,log|a|} with 0<|a|<1. Here the maximum is legal integral PL on the two strict domains cut at |T|=|a|. Its maximum occurs at the actual relative boundary. A boundaryless maximum principle cannot be applied there.

Normalization limitations. The smooth normal unibranch examples in n2 require no normalization. Their existence does not prove normality or unibranchness sufficient for arbitrary higher-dimensional germs. Singular-curve normalization is finite but need not be flat; GJR Proposition 5.11 cannot simply descend strict PL approximants through it. A topological homeomorphism of a normalization likewise does not establish strict membership downstairs. Identifying values of independently chosen branch approximants does not prove monotonicity on one ordinary neighbourhood. No general singular-curve or higher-dimensional normalization criterion is established.

Residue and genus range. The strict star construction of n1 uses integral model functions and real coefficients, not ordinary local logarithmic harmonicity. Positive-genus residue components and nontorsion residue Picard classes are allowed. GJR Remark 15.10 explains that harmonic functions need not be ordinary CLD smooth. Wanner’s cached arXiv:1801.04713v3, Corollary 5.4, page 31, assumes a smooth proper curve and finite continuous starting functions, with residue field algebraic over a finite field or the projective-line/Mumford alternatives for its decreasing ordinary CLD-smooth conclusion. These are comparison facts only. They are not used to add false restrictions to strict real-PL regularization, or to claim ordinary smoothness. No locally Fubini–Study, weakly smooth or CLD-smooth conclusion is made for the present atom.

Remaining original obligations. A sharp characterization for the full arbitrary classical psh germ class in dimension at least two remains unresolved. So do constructions for arbitrary germs in ordinary affine opens of smooth normal unibranch spaces; sharp necessity and genuine failure examples for the regularization property; general normalization descent; unrestricted extraction when second countability is unavailable; curve boundary cases outside the proved range; and general tropical-chart overlap gluing outside the globally pulled-back bundle sector. Neither the F_sigma test nor the shortcut counterexamples establish the sharp failure range. Original P02.1 therefore remains open in this draft, and candidate=false.
